note: Product Anatomy Matrix questions, version 0.x (unevaluated). Each is one typed judgment per product, asked against the company's core product in `core`. Weights live in phases.json, apart from the answers.

promise_delivery.instructions: When the people the core promise is made to use this product, how directly do they get what `core.promise` promises?
criteria: They do not get it from this product at all
They get it only indirectly, through another product or an intermediary
They get part of it directly from this product
They get the whole promise directly from this product

competence_draw.instructions: How much does this product depend on the core competence described in `core.competence`?
criteria: It does not use the core competence
It uses the core competence's outputs now and then
It is built on the core competence and would not work without it
It is the core competence itself, offered as a product

promise_breach.instructions: As described, could this product lead people to receive what `core.must_not` rules out, under the company's name?

criteria.true: Yes: the product's normal use could deliver what the promise rules out
criteria.false: No: its normal use stays within the promise

job_intensity.instructions: How strongly do this product's first users feel the problem it solves?
criteria: A mild preference: they would not change their habits for it
A noticeable annoyance they would fix if it were easy
A real pain they already spend time or money working around
An urgent pain they would adopt an unfinished product to fix

ready.instructions: Given `company.team` and `company.current_state`, how close is this product to being usable by real users?
criteria: It is an idea; most of it would need building with people the company does not have
Parts exist, but it needs major work or people the company does not have
Most of it exists, or it could be built by the current team within a few months
Real users can use it now

revenue.instructions: How strong is this product's own path to revenue, without counting what it does for the other products?
criteria: No credible revenue path
A weak or distant revenue path
A clear revenue path that others in its market already prove
Buyers who would pay now, with a clear price

reversibility.instructions: If the company led with this product and it proved the wrong choice, how easily could it back off?
criteria: Very hard: commitments to customers, contracts or regulators would be broken
Hard: it would cost significant money, trust or time
Moderate: some sunk work and some disappointed users
Easy: little would be lost
